reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the critic judged that the reading misread the request: The reading assumes Athena's checks run before the early pull request call. In the snapshot they run after it. In produce_and_verify (run.rs), the candidate commit is made at 1586-1595, admission and fingerprinting run at 1598-1639, early_pr is called at 1645, and the routed checks (run_routed) start at 1700. The reading itself notes "the checks at about line 1700". So the 12 minutes the request blames are already after the early pull request call. The only work between the commit and the call is admission, fingerprinting, one UI line and remove_tree, which takes seconds. The request's timing figures still need a cause. Code that may explain them: the baseline checks run on the base commit before the producer (run.rs:1345-1366, take_baseline), and landing replaces the early head with a different landing commit (gh.rs:1819-1823 and 1989-2003, replace_early), so CI runs fresh on the landing SHA. The reading does not trace either one. (round 2 of 3). The plan names real code and lines. run.rs:1595 is the candidate tree, 1645 is the early_pr call, and gh.rs:2303 is the early_pr helper. But it rests on a premise the snapshot contradicts: Athena's routed checks start at run.rs:1700, after the existing early_pr call. Moving the call ahead of admission saves seconds, not the 12 minutes the request describes, so the root cause is not addressed. Two leads are visible in the code: the landing commit replacing the early head with a new SHA (gh.rs replace_early), and the early run not finishing before landing began. The criterion 1 test's boundary (the 'candidate …' UI line) measures only the admission ordering, not 'before the checks start'. Pushing before admission also sends personal-data-refused candidates to the remote for no measurable gain. The planner should trace the actual delay, fix it where it starts or name it as outside scope, and make the ordering test observe the start of the checks. Findings: major: The planned move does not change when CI starts relative to Athena's checks; the root cause is somewhere else (Plan Decision 1 / Step 1; run.rs:1595-1700); major: The criterion 1 test uses the 'candidate …' UI line as its boundary, which does not show the call happens before the checks (Demonstrations, criterion 1; Decision 3); minor: Pushing before admission sends refused candidates to the remote, which can include content that admission blocks for personal data or size (Risks / Open questions; run.rs:1598-1607 (personal_data, max_file_bytes)); minor: The admission-refusal never-merged test depends on the risky ordering (Demonstrations, criterion 2(a))
